items.setupText: Choose the summary that preserves the stated reason for setting aside the account without treating lack of support as proof of falsity.

rationales.The account was set aside in order to ob: 'For want of' identifies an existing lack; it does not express a purpose of disproving the account.
rationales.The account was set aside because suppor: 'For want of' means because of a lack of something. The final clause distinguishes missing support from disproof.

items.setupText: Choose the editorial advice that preserves a natural conversational question.
items.taskText: A dialogue contains: 'Which proposal were you referring to?' An editor wants to remove the final to because sentences should not end with a preposition.

Keep to: refer to needs it here, and a final preposition is natural in this dialogue.

items.answer: Keep to: refer to needs it here, and a final preposition is natural in this dialogue.
items.explanation: Preposition stranding is normal in English questions. 'To which proposal were you referring?' is possible but more formal.

rationales.Delete to; referring takes the proposal: For mentioning or alluding to a proposal, the construction is 'refer to', not 'refer a proposal'.
rationales.Keep to: refer to needs it here, and a f: Preposition stranding is normal in English questions. 'To which proposal were you referring?' is possible but more formal.
rationales.Replace to with about because final to i: The position is allowed, and 'referring about' is not the required construction.
rationales.Move to before which because only indire: Direct questions also allow final prepositions; fronting is a style choice here, not a grammatical requirement.

items.setupText: Which assessment of the proposed edit is accurate?

The edit simply unpacks consistent with into a fuller description of the same preference.
The edit excludes the rival explanations as incompatible with the observations.
The edit weakens the original preference by allowing the rival explanations to remain possible.
items.answer: The edit adds a comparative evidential preference that the original explicitly leaves unsupported.

items.setupText: Which interpretation is supported by both clauses?

items.setupText: Choose the most faithful paraphrase of the statement.

items.answer: The archive and a library have comparable access arrangements; the ownership comparison is excluded.

rationales.In view of my reservations, I recommend: This makes the reservations grounds for publication and removes correction as a condition.
rationales.Subject to my reservations, I recommend: This exchanges the roles: reservations become the qualification while uncorrected errors become an obstacle publication proceeds despite.
rationales.Notwithstanding my reservations, I recom: 'Notwithstanding' concedes the continuing reservations; 'subject to' makes correction a condition of the recommendation.
rationales.Following the resolution of my reservati: This claims the reservations were resolved and permits publication before corrections, reversing both parts of the brief.

findings: The original appellate-review gap was basic; the first notwithstanding-versus-because draft still tested only a simple concession reversal.
audit.microSkill: Coordinating concessive notwithstanding with conditional subject to
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates a reservation accepted from a requirement that must still be met.
audit.levelReason: A concise editorial recommendation must preserve two interacting qualifications, appropriate at C2.
audit.similarityNote: Paired concession and condition, not another simple despite synonym.

items.setupText: Choose the rewrite that preserves the original comparison.
items.taskText: 'As against the earlier edition's fuller notes, the new edition offers a more accurate text.'
options: The new edition is preferable to the earlier one because accuracy matters more than notes.
The earlier edition has fuller notes, whereas the new edition has a more accurate text.
The new edition improves both the text and the notes supplied by the earlier edition.
The new edition's more accurate text compensates for its less extensive notes.
items.answer: The earlier edition has fuller notes, whereas the new edition has a more accurate text.
items.explanation: The contrast preserves the distinct quality attributed to each edition without ranking those qualities against each other.

rationales.The new edition is preferable to the ear: This adds a weighting of the two qualities and an overall preference.
rationales.The earlier edition has fuller notes, wh: The contrast preserves the distinct quality attributed to each edition without ranking those qualities against each other.
rationales.The new edition improves both the text a: The original attributes fuller notes to the earlier edition, not improvement in both areas to the new one.
rationales.The new edition's more accurate text com: Compensates for adds a judgment that one advantage offsets the other; the original simply contrasts the two features.

findings: The technical-memorandum analogy gap repeated analogous to without a substantive comparison decision.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Avoids inventing a common scale or overall ranking from distinct advantages.
audit.levelReason: Preserving dimensions and evaluative neutrality in a compact comparison suits C2.
audit.similarityNote: Qualitative comparison without an ordered quantitative relation or common-benchmark inference.

items.setupText: Which revision preserves the original claim?
items.taskText: 'The journalist completed the interview without asking about the disputed donation.'
options: The journalist completed the interview to prevent discussion of the disputed donation.
The journalist completed the interview despite being forbidden to ask about the disputed donation.
The interview was completed with no question from the journalist about the disputed donation.
The journalist completed the interview before being able to ask about the disputed donation.
items.answer: The interview was completed with no question from the journalist about the disputed donation.
items.explanation: This preserves the absent action and its agent without assigning a motive or ruling out other ways the subject arose.

rationales.The journalist completed the interview t: 'To prevent' adds an intention; 'without asking' reports an omission without explaining it.
rationales.The interview was completed with no ques: This preserves the absent action and its agent without assigning a motive or ruling out other ways the subject arose.
rationales.The journalist completed the interview d: This adds a prohibition and presents it as an obstacle, neither of which is stated.
rationales.The journalist completed the interview b: This adds lack of opportunity and implies an intended later question rather than simply reporting the omission.

findings: The accordance item combined elementary form recall with inconsistent past/present sequencing.
audit.microSkill: Absent action without versus purpose and prevented opportunity
audit.pedagogicalValue: Keeps omission distinct from intention, prohibition, and inability.
audit.levelReason: Preserving a negative event description without adding causal psychology suits C2.
audit.similarityNote: Scope of an omitted action, not source attribution or basic without an ingredient.

items.setupText: The author's brief is to evaluate only the book's treatment of sources, praising its clarity and criticizing its brevity. Choose a clear revision.
items.taskText: Draft: 'The review praises the book's clarity and criticizes its brevity in its treatment of sources.'
options: The review praises the book's overall clarity but criticizes the brevity of its treatment of sources.
The review praises the clarity of the book's treatment of sources but criticizes the book's overall brevity.
In assessing the book's treatment of sources, the review praises its clarity and criticizes its brevity.
In assessing the book as a whole, the review praises its clarity and criticizes its brevity.
items.answer: In assessing the book's treatment of sources, the review praises its clarity and criticizes its brevity.
items.explanation: The initial phrase makes source treatment the frame for both evaluations.

rationales.The review praises the book's overall cl: This extends the praise to the whole book while restricting only the criticism to source treatment.
rationales.The review praises the clarity of the bo: This restricts the praise but extends the criticism to the entire book.
rationales.In assessing the book's treatment of sou: The initial phrase makes source treatment the frame for both evaluations.
rationales.In assessing the book as a whole, the re: This applies both judgments to the whole book, exceeding the author's restricted brief.

findings: The lesson-plan consistency gap added a caveat-removal tail but no advanced language demand.
audit.microSkill: Shared scope of a fronted assessment phrase
audit.pedagogicalValue: Moves a qualification so that it clearly applies to two coordinated evaluations.
audit.levelReason: Editing the scope of a modifier across coordination suits C2.
audit.similarityNote: Shared evaluative limitation, not a common existential referent.

items.setupText: Which summary accurately represents the speaker's position?
items.taskText: 'I object to the proposal only to the extent that it transfers editorial decisions to the sponsor; I have no objection to the funding arrangement itself.'
options: The speaker opposes sponsorship unless the sponsor makes the editorial decisions.
The speaker's objection grows whenever the amount of sponsorship increases.
The objection concerns the transfer of editorial decisions, not sponsorship as such.
The speaker accepts the transfer of editorial decisions but objects to its funding.
items.answer: The objection concerns the transfer of editorial decisions, not sponsorship as such.
items.explanation: The phrase restricts the objection to a particular feature, reinforced by explicit acceptance of the funding arrangement itself.

rationales.The speaker opposes sponsorship unless t: This reverses the concern: transferring those decisions is the objectionable feature.
rationales.The speaker's objection grows whenever t: 'To the extent that' here limits the grounds of objection; it does not set a financial scale.
rationales.The objection concerns the transfer of e: The phrase restricts the objection to a particular feature, reinforced by explicit acceptance of the funding arrangement itself.
rationales.The speaker accepts the transfer of edit: This reverses both the disputed and accepted parts of the proposal.

findings: The policy-committee contingency frame repeated a fixed preposition rather than a qualified position.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Interprets a limited objection without turning extent into an amount or reversing its basis.
audit.levelReason: A carefully qualified argumentative stance suits C2.
audit.similarityNote: Scope of grounds for objection, not a numeric threshold.

items.setupText: The writer confirms that both the budget and travel costs were discussed. Choose an explicit revision of the draft.
items.taskText: Draft: 'Apart from the budget, we discussed travel costs.'
options: Excluding the budget, we discussed travel costs.
Instead of the budget, we discussed travel costs.
With regard to the budget, we discussed travel costs.
In addition to the budget, we discussed travel costs.
items.answer: In addition to the budget, we discussed travel costs.
items.explanation: 'Apart from' can be additive or exceptive; 'in addition to' makes the intended inclusion explicit.

rationales.Excluding the budget, we discussed trave: This chooses the exception reading of apart from rather than the intended addition.
rationales.In addition to the budget, we discussed: 'Apart from' can be additive or exceptive; 'in addition to' makes the intended inclusion explicit.
rationales.Instead of the budget, we discussed trav: This replaces the budget as a topic rather than retaining it alongside travel costs.
rationales.With regard to the budget, we discussed: This treats travel costs as a budget-related subtopic, not explicitly as an additional topic discussed.

findings: The ethics-review irrespective-of item repeated form recall and generic feedback.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Clarifies an intended reading without declaring the alternative reading ungrammatical.
audit.levelReason: An editing criterion resolves a genuine lexical ambiguity at C2.
audit.similarityNote: Ambiguity repair, distinct from B2's clearly exceptive flat assessment.

items.setupText: Which summary accurately represents the editor's offer?
items.taskText: 'Short of withdrawing the essay from the collection, I can accommodate the changes you propose,' the editor wrote.
options: The editor can accommodate the changes only after the author withdraws the essay.
The editor offers accommodation in exchange for the author's promise to withdraw the essay.
The editor offers to accommodate changes that stop short of withdrawing the essay.
The editor predicts that the proposed changes will fall short of preventing withdrawal.
items.answer: The editor offers to accommodate changes that stop short of withdrawing the essay.
items.explanation: Here 'short of' marks the boundary of the offer: lesser changes can be accommodated, but withdrawal is not included.

rationales.The editor can accommodate the changes o: This turns the excluded step into a prior condition of accommodating changes.
rationales.The editor offers accommodation in excha: This invents a reciprocal bargain; 'short of' identifies a limit, not an exchange.
rationales.The editor offers to accommodate changes: Here 'short of' marks the boundary of the offer: lesser changes can be accommodated, but withdrawal is not included.
rationales.The editor predicts that the proposed ch: This takes short of as insufficiency for an outcome and turns an offer into a prediction about withdrawal.

findings: The original counterargument-table analogy was repetitive; the initial in-common-with paraphrase was too elementary for C2.
audit.microSkill: Short of as boundary of accommodation versus insufficiency
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes a limit on an offer from a condition, exchange, or prediction of failure.
audit.levelReason: Interpreting a context-sensitive limiting phrase in negotiated editorial language suits C2.
audit.similarityNote: Boundary of accommodation, not a shared property or quantitative limit.

items.setupText: How does the proposed edit affect the meaning?
items.taskText: Original: 'The studio received a grant in recognition of its contribution to local theatre.' Edit: 'The studio received a grant in return for its contribution to local theatre.'
options: The edit presents the grant as an exchange for the contribution, rather than simply an acknowledgement of it.
Both versions give the same reason for the grant; the edit changes only the level of formality.
The edit changes a past contribution into a promise of future theatre work.
The edit changes a reward for past work into payment under a previously agreed bargain.
items.answer: The edit presents the grant as an exchange for the contribution, rather than simply an acknowledgement of it.
items.explanation: In recognition of marks acknowledgement; in return for frames one thing as given in exchange for another.

rationales.Both versions give the same reason for t: Recognition and reciprocal exchange are different meanings, not merely different levels of formality.
rationales.The edit presents the grant as an exchan: In recognition of marks acknowledgement; in return for frames one thing as given in exchange for another.
rationales.The edit changes a past contribution int: In return for does not by itself determine whether the contribution is past or future.
rationales.The edit changes a reward for past work: An exchange framing does not establish that a bargain was agreed in advance.

findings: The pre-adjudication accordance gap repeated an elementary fixed phrase.
audit.microSkill: Acknowledgement in recognition of versus exchange in return for
audit.pedagogicalValue: Detects a change in transactional framing without inventing timing or monetary equivalence.
audit.levelReason: A subtle distinction between institutional rationales suits C2.
audit.similarityNote: Acknowledgement versus exchange, not consent or compliance.

items.setupText: Edit the draft to state when the meeting began. Do not add an explanation for the chair's decision.
items.taskText: Draft: 'With two members still absent, the chair began the meeting.'
options: The chair began the meeting because two members were still absent.
The chair began the meeting while two members were still absent.
The chair began the meeting despite two members still being absent.
The chair began the meeting after two members had left.
items.answer: The chair began the meeting while two members were still absent.
items.explanation: The with phrase supplies a concurrent circumstance; 'while' makes simultaneity explicit without specifying a motive.

rationales.The chair began the meeting because two: This makes the absences the cause of beginning, which the brief leaves open.
rationales.The chair began the meeting despite two: This presents absence as an obstacle overridden; the brief asks to make timing explicit without adding that relationship.
rationales.The chair began the meeting while two me: The with phrase supplies a concurrent circumstance; 'while' makes simultaneity explicit without specifying a motive.
rationales.The chair began the meeting after two me: This adds an earlier departure. The with phrase does not establish that the absent members had previously been there.

findings: The statutory-analysis consistency item added specialist vocabulary without advanced syntax.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Expands a reduced circumstance phrase without unnecessarily adding cause, concession, or purpose.
audit.levelReason: Choosing among plausible discourse expansions under a precise brief suits C2.
audit.similarityNote: Concurrent circumstance, not instrument with or shared modifier scope.

items.setupText: Choose the revision that preserves the statement's meaning.
items.taskText: 'In the critic's reading of the novel, the narrator's politeness is a form of resistance.'
options: The novelist presents politeness as resistance in the critic's account of the novel.
The critic interprets the narrator's politeness as a form of resistance.
The critic reports that the novelist explicitly described politeness as resistance.
The novel confirms the critic's claim that the narrator intended resistance.
items.answer: The critic interprets the narrator's politeness as a form of resistance.
items.explanation: In the critic's reading frames the proposition as an interpretation and identifies whose interpretation it is.

rationales.The novelist presents politeness as resi: This attributes the position to the novelist; the original establishes the critic's interpretation without assigning it to the author.
rationales.The critic reports that the novelist exp: This changes the critic's reading into a report of something the novelist expressly said.
rationales.The critic interprets the narrator's pol: In the critic's reading frames the proposition as an interpretation and identifies whose interpretation it is.
rationales.The novel confirms the critic's claim th: This adds confirmation and character intention beyond the attributed interpretation.

findings: The examination-committee contingency frame was a fourth near-copy of a basic pairing.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Keeps an attributed interpretation separate from authorial endorsement and character intention.
audit.levelReason: Preserving layered literary attribution suits C2.
audit.similarityNote: Prepositional framing of a reading, distinct from pronoun antecedent attribution.

items.setupText: The storage manager is describing a view the archivist would take. Choose a faithful revision of the draft.
items.taskText: Draft: 'From the archivist's perspective, retaining the duplicate files is prudent.'
options: As the archivist would see it, retaining the duplicate files is prudent.
From my perspective as storage manager, retaining the duplicate files is prudent.
According to the archivist's explicit instructions, the duplicate files must be retained.
In agreement with the archivist, I regard retention of the duplicate files as prudent.
items.answer: As the archivist would see it, retaining the duplicate files is prudent.
items.explanation: This preserves the attributed standpoint and its hypothetical framing without claiming the archivist has actually stated the view.

rationales.From my perspective as storage manager,: This transfers the evaluation from the archivist's standpoint to the writer's own professional standpoint.
rationales.As the archivist would see it, retaining: This preserves the attributed standpoint and its hypothetical framing without claiming the archivist has actually stated the view.
rationales.According to the archivist's explicit in: This turns an attributed perspective into documented instructions and changes an evaluation into a requirement.
rationales.In agreement with the archivist, I regar: This adds the writer's endorsement. Attributing a standpoint does not establish agreement with it.

findings: The original compliance-addendum item had an unnatural tail; the initial two-perspective summary was too straightforward for C2.
audit.microSkill: Attributed standpoint versus self-endorsement or explicit instruction
audit.pedagogicalValue: Keeps an imagined professional perspective separate from quotation, authority, and agreement.
audit.levelReason: A constrained viewpoint-preserving edit requires C2 control of attribution and stance.
audit.similarityNote: Standpoint attribution under a writer-identity constraint, not simply contrasting two opinions.

items.setupText: Which assessment of the change is accurate?
items.taskText: Original: 'On reading the manuscript, the editor requested a second opinion.' Proposed edit: 'For the purpose of requesting a second opinion, the editor read the manuscript.'
options: The edit changes a response following the reading into a purpose attributed to the reading.
The edit keeps the sequence and merely makes the editor's original purpose explicit.
The edit changes a request made after reading into a request made before reading.
The edit preserves two completed actions while making their connection more explicit.
items.answer: The edit changes a response following the reading into a purpose attributed to the reading.
items.explanation: On reading links the request to the occasion of reading; the purpose phrase instead supplies an aim motivating the reading.

rationales.The edit keeps the sequence and merely m: The original reports a request on reading; it does not say the editor read with that purpose already in mind.
rationales.The edit changes a request made after re: The purpose phrase does not establish that a request was actually made before the reading.
rationales.The edit preserves two completed actions: Reading for the purpose of requesting does not itself report that the request was subsequently made.
rationales.The edit changes a response following th: On reading links the request to the occasion of reading; the purpose phrase instead supplies an aim motivating the reading.

findings: The longitudinal-model analogy item repeated analogous to and relied on technical vocabulary for difficulty.
audit.microSkill: On plus gerund as occasion versus purpose
audit.pedagogicalValue: Avoids recasting a response as an intention that motivated the preceding action.
audit.levelReason: An editorial distinction between temporal occasion and attributed purpose suits C2.
audit.similarityNote: Occasion of response, unlike the C1 explicit with-a-view-to purpose.

items.setupText: The curator discussed the loans with the northern and southern museums. Only the northern museum was involved in correspondence.
items.taskText: Which sentence accurately combines these facts?
options: The curator discussed the loans and corresponded with both museums.
With both museums, the curator discussed the loans and maintained correspondence.
The curator discussed the loans with the northern museum and corresponded with both museums.
The curator discussed the loans with both museums and corresponded with the northern museum.
items.answer: The curator discussed the loans with both museums and corresponded with the northern museum.
items.explanation: Repeating 'with' assigns each verb its own participants: both museums for discussion, only the northern one for correspondence.

rationales.The curator discussed the loans and corr: The shared final phrase makes correspondence involve both museums, exceeding the brief.
rationales.The curator discussed the loans with bot: Repeating 'with' assigns each verb its own participants: both museums for discussion, only the northern one for correspondence.
rationales.With both museums, the curator discussed: The fronted phrase frames both coordinated activities with both museums, losing the unequal coverage.
rationales.The curator discussed the loans with the: This reverses which activity involves both museums and narrows the discussion incorrectly.

findings: The final accordance gap combined elementary recall with a confusing pre-ruling court-order tail.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Uses repeated prepositional phrases to preserve different participant sets for two actions.
audit.levelReason: Editing coordination while retaining unequal complement scope suits C2.
audit.similarityNote: Different coverage for coordinated actions, not a shared witness or quantitative paraphrase.
